question: Dandi March was a journey of _______ miles (approximately) on foot to the salt mines in Gujarat.
solution:
The correct answer is__** 240 miles**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Dandi March**, also known as the Salt March, was a significant event in the Indian independence movement led by **Mahatma Gandhi in 1930**.
 
• The march covered a distance of approximately **240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad to the coastal village of Dandi**.
 
• The journey took 24 days, **starting on March 12, 1930, and concluding on April 6, 1930**.
 
• During the march, Gandhi and his followers protested against **the British salt monopoly and the salt tax imposed on Indians.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Context**: The Dandi March was part of the larger Civil Disobedience Movement, which aimed to resist British laws peacefully.
 
• **Impact on Indian Independence**: The march galvanized Indian citizens against British rule, inspiring mass participation in the struggle for independence.
 
• **Gandhi's Philosophy**: The march exemplified Gandhi's philosophy of non-violence (Ahinsa) and civil disobedience.
 
• **Legacy**: The Dandi March is remembered as a pivotal moment in India's fight for freedom and is celebrated annually as Salt Satyagraha Day.
